title: Effect 4.0 Ships: Dependency-Free Rewrite with 5x Smaller Bundles and Long-Term Support
summary:
Effect 4.0, a TypeScript framework for typed errors and structured concurrency, was released on 30 September 2026 with a rewritten fiber runtime. The team reports a bundle size drop from 35.6 kB to 7.1 kB and about 6.4x higher throughput, though these figures are not independently verified. It also adds long-term support through September 2029.

By Daniel Curtis

title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics Control, Simulation, and Policy Improvement
summary:
Google has released Gemini 4 Argon framing it as a general-purpose physical-reasoning model for robot control, Real2Sim scene construction, multimodal labeling of robot video, and iterative policy improvement, rather than as a single end-effector policy.

By Daniel Dominguez

title: Cloudflare Develops Public Certificate Authority for Post-Quantum Web Security
summary:
Cloudflare is developing a public certificate authority for Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs) to reduce the bandwidth overhead of post-quantum cryptography. A Chrome experiment served billions of MTCs to 50% of Chrome Beta 146 for selected domains, reporting 9% faster median performance. Wider deployment depends on browser support, transparency, and production-scale validation.

By Leela Kumili

title: Podcast: Distributed LLM Inference on Kubernetes with llm-d, Wasm, & TornadoVM
summary:
In this episode, Edoardo Vacchi discusses the evolving landscape of WebAssembly on the backend, running Java workloads on GPUs using TornadoVM, and optimizing distributed AI inference using llm-d and vLLM on Kubernetes. Edoardo explains how llm-d manages cache locality (KV and prefix caches), request routing, and batch inference across Kubernetes clusters to maximize expensive GPU utilization.

By Edoardo Vacchi

title: Article: Agentic AI Architecture: Current Challenges and Future Opportunities
summary:
Agentic AI architecture extends microservices and cloud-native architectures with AI agents that work with context, memory, and protocols such as MCP and A2A. The article covers bounded-context integration, task-dependent coordination strategies, new security risks, and observability needs. It expects gradual adoption alongside existing architectures, with platforms absorbing common components.

By Rafał Gancarz

title: Tokio Releases Topcoat: A Batteries-Included Full-Stack Rust Framework
summary:
Topcoat is an open-source, server-rendered full-stack web framework for Rust from the Tokio team, now public at version 0.9. It uses Rust expressions translated to JavaScript for reactivity instead of WebAssembly. It targets typical database-driven apps. Releases are unstable, and authentication and background jobs remain on the roadmap.

By Daniel Curtis

title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
summary:
Entire is a Git forge designed specifically for collaboration between human developers and AI coding agents. Its premise is that traditional software development infrastructure, particularly the pull request (PR) model, is not well suited to an environment where AI agents generate, review, and iterate on code at high speed.

By Sergio De Simone

title: Google Cloud Adds Self-Managed VMware Cloud Foundation on Bare Metal
summary:
Google Cloud has made a self-managed VMware solution generally available, running VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x on dedicated Z3 bare metal with root access across ESXi, vCenter and NSX in 22 regions. It sits beside the Google-managed VMware Engine and matches customer-operated offerings from AWS and Oracle, shifting lifecycle, patching and Broadcom licensing back to the customer.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: How Grab Improved Mobile App Stability by Safely Handling Surge in AI-Generated Code Changes
summary:
The growing adoption of AI coding assistants has accelerated development and increased the volume of code changes per release, bringing more opportunities for defects and crashes, says Grab. To address these challenges, they implemented a layered defense strategy to prevent, detect, and contain crashes throughout the development and release lifecycle.

By Sergio De Simone

title: Open Source pg_vectorsearch Brings More Scalable Vector Search to PostgreSQL
summary:
Tiger Data has released pg_vectorsearch, an open source PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search, currently in alpha. Its PRISM index uses data partitioning and compression instead of the graph-based approach used by pgvector’s HNSW index, reducing memory requirements and index build times.

By Renato Losio

title: Varlock Releases Bumpy: a File-Based Versioning Alternative to Changesets
summary:
Bumpy is an MIT-licensed, TypeScript tool for version management and changelogs in monorepos. It follows the changesets workflow, using markdown bump files, and adds support for workspace and catalog protocols, custom publish commands, and branch-based prereleases. Changesets v3, released in August 2026, closed many earlier gaps, though differences remain.

By Daniel Curtis
